title: Students and teachers call nationwide strikes and rallies over university funding

tea.why: Protesters say years of austerity have weakened universities, labs, and support services, and government responses are insufficient.
tea.want: 150,000 new higher education places, the repeal of Parcoursup and Mon Master, increased funding, and higher staff salaries and student grants.
tea.changed: Nov 23: An inter-union coalition of higher education unions and student groups called for a nationwide mobilisation and strike day on Nov 26.

summary: Following two months of protests, an inter-union coalition representing higher education staff and students has called for a nationwide day of strikes and demonstrations on November 26, 2026. Organised by groups including FSU, Unsa, CGT, Sud, FO, Unef, Union étudiante, FSE, Fage, Solidaires étudiants, and Interfac Île-de-France, the action aims to pressure the government over university funding and conditions. The participants demand the creation of 150,000 higher education places, a multi-year recruitment plan, higher salaries and grants, and the abolition of the Parcoursup and Mon Master admission platforms. The government responded by announcing 20,000 extra university places, indexing grants to inflation, and planning to reform and replace Parcoursup by 2028, measures the unions dismissed as inadequate.
demands: Implement a multi-year recruitment and tenure plan
Increase funding for public universities and laboratories
Revalue student grants and staff salaries
response: The government announced plans to create 20,000 extra higher education places, index student grants to inflation, and reform Parcoursup starting in 2027 before replacing it in 2028. Unions stated these measures are insufficient.

updates.text: Interfac Île-de-France announced a student mobilisation date for Paris on November 26 during a previous march.
An inter-union coalition of higher education staff and student organisations issued a joint call for nationwide strikes and rallies on November 26.
